name: The Tham Luang cave rescue
label: Thousands of strangers worked to free 13 trapped in a Thai cave, 2018
summary: In June 2018 twelve boys and their soccer coach were trapped by flooding in the Tham Luang cave in northern Thailand. Thai Navy SEALs, international cave divers, doctors, engineers and thousands of volunteers worked to pump out water and bring them out, and all 13 came out alive. Local rice farmers let their fields be flooded by the pumped water, and former Thai Navy SEAL Saman Kunan died while delivering air tanks into the cave.
caveat: Counts of volunteers vary (National Geographic cites a diver's estimate of more than 7,000; other reports say up to 10,000). Whether the farmers asked for compensation is reported differently, and National Geographic says hundreds lost crops and asked for none. Kunan's name is spelled Kunan or Gunan, and BenarNews gives his age as 38 and his cause as losing consciousness after laying tanks; National Geographic says no one knows how or why he died. The pumping diverted water, and the farmers' role was a loss they accepted, not a planned gift.
